\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{محاكمة} (muḥākama)}{محاكمة (muḥākama)}]{\ar{محاكمة} (muḥākama) — a trial}

\label{lesson:AR-C334-muhakama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a pirate, then the Arabic for to capture.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{محاكمة}}
\textbf{\ar{محاكمة}} — \emph{muḥākama} — \textquotedblleft{}a trial\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{بدأت} \ar{محاكمة} \ar{الرجل} \ar{أمس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{badaʾat muḥākamat ar-rajul ams.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The man’s trial began yesterday.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{محاكمة}} (\emph{muḥākama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-k-m} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to judge\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Muḥākama} is the verbal noun of Form III, \textquotedblleft{}to bring someone to judgment\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muḥākama}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muḥākama}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{badaʾat muḥākamat ar-rajul ams.} — The man’s trial began yesterday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a pirate, then the Arabic for to capture, then say \emph{muḥākama} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{محاكمة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A trial\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{جلسة} (jalsa)}{جلسة (jalsa)}]{\ar{جلسة} (jalsa) — a hearing, a session}

\label{lesson:AR-C334-jalsa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to capture, then the Arabic for a trial.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{جلسة}}
\textbf{\ar{جلسة}} — \emph{jalsa} — \textquotedblleft{}a hearing, a session\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تأجلت} \ar{جلسة} \ar{المحكمة} \ar{أسبوعا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taʾajjalat jalsat al-maḥkama usbūʿan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The court hearing was put off for a week.
\end{quote}

Any sitting: \ar{جلسة} \ar{عمل}, a working session.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{جلسة}} (\emph{jalsa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-l-s} (Lane), the root of the taught \emph{jalasa}, to sit. The \emph{faʿla} pattern gives one sitting.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jalsa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jalsa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʾajjalat jalsat al-maḥkama usbūʿan.} — The court hearing was put off for a week.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to capture, then the Arabic for a trial, then say \emph{jalsa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{جلسة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A hearing, a session\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{دفاع} (difāʿ)}{دفاع (difāʿ)}]{\ar{دفاع} (difāʿ) — the defence}

\label{lesson:AR-C334-difa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a trial, then the Arabic for a hearing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{دفاع}}
\textbf{\ar{دفاع}} — \emph{difāʿ} — \textquotedblleft{}the defence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تكلم} \ar{محامي} \ar{الدفاع} \ar{طويلا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{takallama muḥāmī ad-difāʿ ṭawīlan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The defence lawyer spoke for a long time.
\end{quote}

In sport and in war too: \ar{خط} \ar{الدفاع}, the line of defence.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{دفاع}} (\emph{difāʿ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-f-ʿ} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to push\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Difāʿ} is the verbal noun of Form III \emph{dāfaʿa}, \textquotedblleft{}to push back\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{difāʿ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{difāʿ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{takallama muḥāmī ad-difāʿ ṭawīlan.} — The defence lawyer spoke for a long time.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a trial, then the Arabic for a hearing, then say \emph{difāʿ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{دفاع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The defence\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أدان} (adāna)}{أدان (adāna)}]{\ar{أدان} (adāna) — to convict; to condemn}

\label{lesson:AR-C334-adana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a hearing, then the Arabic for the defence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أدان}}
\textbf{\ar{أدان}} — \emph{adāna} — \textquotedblleft{}to convict; to condemn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أدانت} \ar{المحكمة} \ar{الرجل} \ar{بالسرقة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{adānat al-maḥkama ar-rajul bi-s-sariqa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The court convicted the man of theft.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يدين}, \emph{yudīn}.

Of words: \ar{أدان} \ar{الهجوم}, he condemned the attack.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أدان}} (\emph{adāna}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-y-n} (Lane), the root of \emph{dayn}, a debt, and of a judgment that is owed. Modern Arabic gives Form IV \emph{adāna} the sense \textquotedblleft{}to find guilty\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adāna}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adāna}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adānat al-maḥkama ar-rajul bi-s-sariqa.} — The court convicted the man of theft.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a hearing, then the Arabic for the defence, then say \emph{adāna} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أدان} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To convict; to condemn\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{براءة} (barāʾa)}{براءة (barāʾa)}]{\ar{براءة} (barāʾa) — innocence}

\label{lesson:AR-C334-baraa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for the defence, then the Arabic for to convict.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{براءة}}
\textbf{\ar{براءة}} — \emph{barāʾa} — \textquotedblleft{}innocence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أعلن} \ar{القاضي} \ar{براءة} \ar{الشاب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aʿlana al-qāḍī barāʾat ash-shābb.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The judge declared the young man innocent.
\end{quote}

A patent is \ar{براءة} \ar{اختراع}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{براءة}} (\emph{barāʾa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-r-ʾ} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to be free, clear of a thing\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Barāʾa} is being clear of blame.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{barāʾa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{barāʾa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aʿlana al-qāḍī barāʾat ash-shābb.} — The judge declared the young man innocent.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for the defence, then the Arabic for to convict, then say \emph{barāʾa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{براءة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Innocence\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
